newsitem.title: TAIWAN: POLL-Taiwan June trade surplus seen up 20 pct y/y.
newsitem.headline: POLL-Taiwan June trade surplus seen up 20 pct y/y.

text.p: A Reuters Poll of Taiwan economists on Thursday projected trade surplus of US$492 million for Taiwan in June, up 20 percent from a US$410 million surplus in June 1996.
The poll projected that June exports will have grown an annual 3.07 percent and imports an annual 2.32 percent.
Official figures were to be issued by the Finance Ministry at 0245 on July 7.
The following table lists institutions' forecasts for year-on-year growth in June of Taiwan's exports and imports and the resulting trade balance:
Institution Exports chg Imports chg Balance chg
Nomura Securities 9.8 1.09 9.6 3.4 0.2 (51.22)

NOTE: Figures are in billion of U.S. dollars. Change is year-on-year percentage change. Brackets ( ) indicate negative growth. Dash -- indicates no comparison because of deficit against surplus or the other way around:
May showed a trade surplus of US$1.599 billion, with exports at US$10.161 billion and imports at US$8.562 billion.
In June 1996, exports were US$9.695 billion and imports were US$9.285 billion, giving a trade surplus of US$410 million.
Economists noted persistent slow but stable growth in both exports and imports in June.
"Stable growth in foreign orders in the March to May period should be able to support steady export growth in June," said Grand Cathay Securities economist Chang Jui-hsing.
A gradual Taiwan dollar depreciation in May and June would also help Taiwan's export competitiveness.
"The recent Taiwan dollar depreciation should help our export competitivness, but the impact will be clearer in July or August," said Nomura Securities economist Amy Huang.
The Taiwan dollar had depreciated to an eight-year closing low of T$27.92 in mid-June against the greenback from T$27.66 in early May and T$27.34 in mid-January.
It was trading between T$27.850 and T$27.870 on Thursday.
HSBC James Capel economist Stephen Wang was more pessimistic about June's export and import performance.
"Mainland China's demand was still pretty slow, and foreign orders for our information and electronic products seemed to have slowed growth in the second quarter," Wang said.
Most economists said they expected a strong recovery for information technology and electronics exports in the third quarter, which would help to boost overall export performance.
-- Taipei Newsroom (2-5080815)
